note: Existing-source public educational gallery: CC photos and explicitly credited Bob Harms science/education-only photographs are distinguished. Source labels and arrows are not independent specimen voucher certification.

tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
tiles.details: Look for a perennial clump with a contracted terminal or upper-sheath-enclosed panicle. Iowa's grass treatment describes flowering heads about 5–26 cm long and 0.5–1.5 cm wide with branches appressed to the axis. The existing Harms SPCOD3 and SPCOM photographs represent TWO source-labelled varieties; they are not interchangeable Hays vouchers. Head outline cannot separate rough dropseed.
tiles.short: A persistent tuft and crowded, narrow panicle
tiles.status: PANICLE PHOTO PRESENT; LOCAL ROOTED VOUCHER MISSING

tiles.heading: 02 · GROWTH FORM AND LIGULE
tiles.details: Culms commonly 45–130 cm in the Iowa treatment, with a true ligule of fine hairs approximately 0.1–0.5 mm at the inner blade/sheath junction. Variety macer has documented creeping scaly RHIZOMES in Harms SPCOM-8; do NOT teach rhizomes as universal for the whole species. Existing photos do not resolve individual ligule hairs at calibrated magnification.
tiles.status: VAR. MACER RHIZOME VISIBLE; MEASURED LIGULE MISSING

tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE ONE MATURE SPIKELET
tiles.details: A ripe composite-dropseed spikelet is generally single-flowered, laterally compressed, and AWNLESS. The Iowa treatment reports approximately 4.5–5.4 mm, while broader regional concepts include wider values. The Harms SPCOD3-J1 and SPCOM-j1 show real spikelet units but not a detached, independently measured complete glume/lemma/palea series.
tiles.short: One floret; approximately 4.5–5.4 mm in Iowa key

tiles.heading: 04 · GLUMES AND LEMMA
tiles.details: Iowa grass treatment: lower glume approximately 2.6–3.5 mm, upper glume 3.2–4.8 mm, both usually one-veined; fertile lemma approximately 4.4–5.2 mm, smooth, one-veined and awnless; palea 3.9–4.9 mm, two-veined. These are published measurements, NOT measurements of the existing photographs. Photograph separate mature bracts with a 1-mm scale before placing organ-specific arrows.
tiles.short: Two shorter glumes, smooth one-veined lemma

tiles.heading: 05 · SEED TEST IS A HOLD
tiles.details: Some Harms/USFS accounts describe a mature composite-dropseed pericarp that gelatinizes or slips on wetting, whereas a Go Botany key assigns conflicting wet-pericarp states. Preserve this source disagreement and species/variety concepts. Do NOT identify a field plant by an unverified water-drop test or label any existing dry seed photo as gelatinized. Require independent voucher, timed fresh-seed series and source reconciliation.
tiles.short: Conflicting wet-pericarp literature: do not teach a binary test
tiles.status: CONFLICT HELD; NO CERTIFIED WET TEST

tiles.heading: 06 · SEPARATE THE THREE DROPSEEDS
tiles.details: S. clandestinus is another perennial with a tightly contracted panicle; it requires mature glume/lemma and specialist lemma-surface/pericarp work for reliable separation. S. vaginiflorus is generally an annual with terminal and upper-sheath flowering; other dropseeds may also hide flowers. The Harms SPCOD3-v right panel is S. clandestinus, NOT composite dropseed. Record Sporobolus sp. if no mature diagnostic evidence.
tiles.short: Perennial rough dropseed and annual poverty dropseed
tiles.status: COMPARISONS DOCUMENTED; MATCHED REPRODUCTIVE MACROS MISSING

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: COMPOSITE DROPSEED (*Sporobolus compositus* sensu lato): follow the persistent perennial clump, then a narrowly contracted sometimes partially upper-sheath-enclosed terminal PANICLE of many AWNLESS one-flowered spikelets. The new Bob Harms photographic lessons come from TWO clearly labelled forms: *S. compositus var. drummondii* (SPCOD3-b/i/J0/J1/v; the v side-by-side RIGHT is actually *S. clandestinus*) and *S. compositus var. macer* (SPCOM-b/j1/8). SPCOD3-J0 shows original purple exserted flowering organs, J1 true spikelet-bearing close axis, i open/closed panicle contrast, while SPCOM-8 shows REAL attached scale-covered underground RHIZOME of var. macer ONLY. These features do NOT settle all varieties or *S. clandestinus* separation. Verify an actual rooted specimen and measured intact glumes, smooth lemma surface, and mature pericarp response before species-level final certification.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 2 · Examine the whole plant
steps.look_for: 1. ROOT/CROWN: use original Cody Stricker green head and genuine Harms drummondii b multi-culm sections to recognize growth architecture; do not call an unrooted panicle a true whole plant.
steps.why_it_matters: Habit and growing context are supporting evidence, not proof of hidden roots or rhizomes.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: Culms commonly 45–130 cm in the Iowa treatment, with a true ligule of fine hairs approximately 0.1–0.5 mm at the inner blade/sheath junction. Variety macer has documented creeping scaly RHIZOMES in Harms SPCOM-8; do NOT teach rhizomes as universal for the whole species. Existing photos do not resolve individual ligule hairs at calibrated magnification.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: A ripe composite-dropseed spikelet is generally single-flowered, laterally compressed, and AWNLESS. The Iowa treatment reports approximately 4.5–5.4 mm, while broader regional concepts include wider values. The Harms SPCOD3-J1 and SPCOM-j1 show real spikelet units but not a detached, independently measured complete glume/lemma/palea series.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

The new Bob Harms photographic lessons come from TWO clearly labelled forms: *S. compositus var. drummondii* (SPCOD3-b/i/J0/J1/v; the v side-by-side RIGHT is actually *S. clandestinus*) and *S. compositus var. macer* (SPCOM-b/j1/8). SPCOD3-J0 shows original purple exserted flowering organs, J1 true spikelet-bearing close axis, i open/closed panicle contrast, while SPCOM-8 shows REAL attached scale-covered underground RHIZOME of var. macer ONLY. These features do NOT settle all varieties or *S. clandestinus* separation. Verify an actual rooted specimen and measured intact glumes, smooth lemma surface, and mature pericarp response before species-level final certification.
memory_rule: COMPOSITE DROPSEED COMPLEX: persistent PERENNIAL crown, narrow partly SHEATHED PANICLE of awnless ONE-FLORET spikelets. Bob Harms labels var. drummondii and var. macer separately; macer has pictured RHIZOMES but 'all composite dropseed is rhizomatous' is FALSE. Real lemma and pericarp micro separates from S. clandestinus, not head posture.
safety_note: Bob Harms source photographs show *S. compositus var. drummondii* OR *var. macer*, which may be treated differently in floras. The source comparison v includes the different species *S. clandestinus*. Do not interpret macer rhizome as universal or pretend a wet grain pericarp experiment was photographed.
field_rule: Use visible macro morphology first and defer difficult perennial-species separations to mature material, reliable grain tests and microscope when necessary.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
